research.job_description_summary: Infosys hires freshers (BE/B.Tech/ME/M.Tech/MCA/MSc, 2024-2026 batches, 60% or 6.0 CGPA, no active backlogs) as Systems Engineer, Specialist Programmer and Digital Specialist Engineer. Secondary sources describe an online test (aptitude, reasoning, pseudocode, and DSA coding for Specialist Programmer; Automata Fix for Digital Specialist Engineer), a technical interview (programming, DBMS, OS, project) and an HR interview. Training is at the Mysuru campus.
limitations: The official Infosys pages that could be fetched (infosys.com careers and graduates pages, last modified 2026-05-05) name programmes such as HackWithInfy, InfyTQ and Power Programmers but list no fresher roles, rounds or eligibility; the role and process description comes from a secondary aggregator (freshershunt.in, 2026-06-23), which also says the drive had closed.

The largest candidate-reported source is an anonymous aggregate on freshershunt.in (published 2026-08-19, 220 questions, 1,097 citations). Counts are user-submitted estimates; some entries are garbled, and several listed questions show no count (recorded as at least one report).
placementpreparation.io content is labelled 'sample questions' and is not attributed to candidates; it was used only as topic context.
No question reports specific to Specialist Programmer or Digital Specialist Engineer were found; those tracks use original practice questions (class D) mapped to the described focus areas.
The 2026 aptitude, pseudocode and debugging items are original practice items, not reported questions.
Package figures differ between sources and were not used.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

questions.prompt: This function should return the sum of the first n natural numbers but gives the wrong answer. Find and fix the bug. def total(n): s = 0; for i in range(1, n): s += i; return s
questions.relevance_to_role: A secondary source lists pseudocode and Automata Fix debugging for Digital Specialist Engineer assessments.
questions.expected_answer: range(1, n) stops at n-1, so n is never added. Fix: range(1, n + 1), or use n*(n+1)//2.
follow_ups: What does total(0) return after the fix?
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/infosys/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the bug: def is_pal(s): i = 0; j = len(s); while i < j: if s[i] != s[j]: return False; i += 1; j -= 1; return True

questions.expected_answer: j starts at len(s), which is out of range and raises IndexError. Fix: j = len(s) - 1.
follow_ups: How does your fix behave for an empty string?

questions.subtopic: Second largest value and its position
questions.prompt: Find the second largest distinct value in an array and the 1-based position of its first occurrence.
questions.relevance_to_role: Second-largest-element programs are reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Track max and second max; then locate the first occurrence.
follow_ups: How would you find the k-th largest?
questions.notes: The source reports 'second-largest element'; the index requirement is an original extension.

coding.problem_statement: Given n integers, print the second largest distinct value and the 1-based index of its first occurrence, separated by a space. Print -1 if no second distinct value exists.
coding.expected_algorithm: Single pass tracking top two distinct values.

questions.prompt: Check whether a number is a perfect number, meaning it equals the sum of its proper divisors.
questions.relevance_to_role: Perfect-number programs are reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Loop i up to sqrt(n), adding i and n/i when i divides n (avoid double counting squares).
follow_ups: How would you list all perfect numbers below 10^4?
common_mistakes: Including n itself in the sum

coding.problem_statement: Given n, print Yes if the sum of its proper divisors (excluding n) equals n, otherwise No.

questions.expected_answer: Build the reversed number using rev = rev*10 + n%10 on the absolute value.

coding.problem_statement: Given an integer n, print the number formed by reversing its digits. Keep the sign. Leading zeros of the result are dropped.

questions.prompt: What is a constructor? Can constructors be overloaded or private?
questions.relevance_to_role: Constructors are reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: A constructor initialises a new object and shares the class name (no return type). Constructors can be overloaded; a private constructor prevents outside instantiation, used by singletons and utility classes.
follow_ups: Can a constructor be inherited or abstract?
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: How does exception handling work? Explain try, catch, finally and when you would throw your own exception.
questions.relevance_to_role: Exception handling is reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Code that may fail goes in try; catch handles specific exception types; finally runs cleanup in all cases. Throw custom exceptions to signal domain errors that callers should handle.
follow_ups: What is the difference between throw and throws?
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: What is a pointer? Explain a null pointer, a dangling pointer and a pointer to a pointer.
questions.relevance_to_role: Pointers are reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: A pointer stores a memory address. A null pointer points to nothing; a dangling pointer refers to memory that has been freed or gone out of scope; a pointer to a pointer stores the address of another pointer, used for dynamic 2D arrays or modifying a pointer inside a function.
follow_ups: How can you avoid a dangling pointer?
common_mistakes: Saying a null pointer is uninitialised garbage
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: Explain supervised and unsupervised learning, and how you would detect and reduce overfitting.
questions.relevance_to_role: The Digital Specialist Engineer track is described as AI/ML, cloud and data science by a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: Supervised learning trains on labelled data (classification, regression); unsupervised finds structure in unlabelled data (clustering). Overfitting shows as low training error but high validation error; reduce it with more data, regularisation, simpler models, dropout and cross-validation.
follow_ups: What metric would you use for an imbalanced classification problem?

questions.prompt: Explain IaaS, PaaS and SaaS with an example of each.

questions.expected_answer: IaaS provides virtual infrastructure (virtual machines); PaaS provides a managed platform for deploying code; SaaS delivers complete applications over the web. Example: a virtual machine, a managed app platform, and a web email service.
follow_ups: Who manages the operating system in each model?

questions.prompt: A dataset has missing values in several columns. How would you decide what to do about them?
questions.relevance_to_role: Data science is listed as a Digital Specialist Engineer focus area by a secondary source.
questions.expected_answer: Check the pattern and amount of missingness. Drop rows or columns only if few or irrelevant; otherwise impute (mean or median for numerics, mode for categories, or model-based) and add a missing-indicator when missingness is informative. Validate that imputation does not leak test data.
follow_ups: When is the median better than the mean?
